analysis: All changes in this batch are documentation only. The PR documents a separate install identity for dev builds. These docs live at docs/developer/build.md (new Dev Build Identity section, lines 108-129 at head) and docs/operations/provider-release.md (patch hunk adding the Dev Build Identity subsection). The dev build gets its own CLI name (darkbloom-dev), app bundle, data and config directories, LaunchAgent labels, port 8101 and keychain service/key-label prefix. The code-signing identifier io.darkbloom.provider, the keychain access group SLDQ2GJ6TL.io.darkbloom.provider, the MDM profile identifiers and the fan helper io.darkbloom.fan-helper are explicitly kept identical across prod and dev, so the App Attest/Developer ID/provisioning bindings (TB-011, A-015..A-017) are unchanged. The docs state that the coordinator release registration still requires the bin/darkbloom, bin/darkbloom-enclave and bundle names. The documented fan helper is a single shared system service (TB-010/T-044..T-047 unaffected by the docs). The documented runtime-smoke line now includes cli=<darkbloom|darkbloom-dev>. The identity-binding.md change is a pure link-pin or table-text edit with no behavioral claims altered. I verified none of the source files these docs describe (Package.swift, BuildEnvironment.swift, scripts/provider_release_identity.py, scripts/install.sh select_provider_identity), so the documented behavior is unconfirmed. Later passes should check those files if they appear in the PR. In particular, check that a dev-keychain prefix cannot cross-read prod SE keys (A-002/T-035). Also check that the shared keychain access group does not let dev builds access prod items, and that the dev updater/installer cannot be steered to the prod coordinator or vice versa (A-011, TB-002). No findings from this documentation-only batch.
